"Item 8" with the same labels the data frame uses as column names, ultimately after Bartholomew, Steel, Moustaki & Galbraith 2002). The Bangladesh Fertility Survey 1989 interviewed rural Bangladeshi women, so the administered wording was almost certainly Bengali; no Bengali original is present in the source (the ltm package is the whole deposit -- the dictionary URL is the CRAN page) and no BFS 1989 questionnaire was locatable, so this is the English-substitute fallback: language=Bengali, base fields English, _translated columns empty. The administered-language inference is not documented anywhere in scope and is flagged here as an inference, not a finding. "instructions" is the documentation's third-person description of what respondents were asked ("Women were asked whether they could engage in the following activities alone"), reworded only by dropping the parenthetical coding legend (1 = yes, 0 = no), which is carried in option_text instead; it is not a verbatim administered instruction and none exists in scope. No rights restriction found: the items are 1989 national-survey questions redistributed in a GPL (>= 2) CRAN package, no rights holder statement of any kind was locatable, so under "silence is permission" this ships.

AN INCIDENTAL DATA FINDING, recorded because it is worth knowing whether or not item text ever ships: the deposited resp values are NOT plain agreement, contradicting the paper's 'six-point Likert scale, ranging from 6 (strongly agree) to 1 (strongly disagree)'. The xlsx's own Sharing/Caring/Overall columns are exact raw sums of the 18 deposited columns (least-squares weights 1/0 to 1e-15 over 217 complete rows; Sharing = items 1,4,5,8,9,10,12,15,18, Caring = 2,3,6,7,11,13,14,16,17), and those sums reproduce the paper's Table 1 (my Year-2 n=142: Sharing 3.249+-0.526, Caring 4.081+-0.519, Overall 3.665+-0.429 vs published n=141 3.23+-0.53 / 4.06+-0.53 / 3.64+-0.44). Read as agreement, the patient-centeredness direction would give Caring 3.44 < Sharing 3.73, reversing the universally replicated caring>sharing pattern; read as already reverse-scored it gives 4.08 > 3.25, which matches. Consistent with that, items 9, 13 and 17 -- the only three patient-centered-WORDED items -- are the only three with near-zero or negative item-total r (+0.066, +0.141, -0.089 against +0.25..+0.57 for the other 15). What that evidence cannot settle is whether the flip was blanket (all 18) or selective (the 15 doctor-centered items only), i.e. what resp=6 means for items 9/13/17, so had this table shipped, option_text would have been left blank for all six levels with the form's printed anchor words (Strongly agree / Somewhat agree / Agree / Disagree / Somewhat disagree / Strongly disagree) quoted only in a public_note. RETRY TEST: NO. Determinate verdict -- the licence reserves a right (permission required from the rights holder), which is not an access failure. Nothing about the sources is unresolved: the wording, the codes and the mapping were all recovered. What would flip it: Krupat or a successor publishing terms that permit redistribution of the wording, or Ben ruling that a permission-required clause evidenced only through a third-party measures library plus acknowledgement sections is not enough to block. ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION (Step 5b re-check, 2026-09-09): the structural half of this incidental scoring finding reproduces EXACTLY -- Sharing, Caring and Overall in peerj-12-18676-s001.xlsx are exact raw sums of the 18 PPOS columns (maxdiff 0 over 262 complete rows; Sharing = items 1,4,5,8,9,10,12,15,18). The item-total arithmetic in the extractor's note does NOT reproduce and should not be relied on. Recomputed on the deposit: SIX items, not three, have near-zero or negative corrected item-total r -- 9:-0.130, 10:+0.106, 13:+0.075, 14:+0.135, 17:-0.195, 18:+0.089, against +0.261..+0.420 for the other twelve (identical whether or not the summary columns are required non-missing). The note's figures (+0.066/+0.141/-0.089 for 9/13/17, 'the only three') are wrong, and its 'Year 2, n=142 -> 3.249/4.081/3.665' is not reachable from this file: Year==2 has 128 rows, 121 complete, giving Sharing/9=3.398, Caring/9=3.757, Overall/18=3.577. So the DIRECTION of the finding stands -- a scoring-direction anomaly is real, and the low-discriminating items are drawn from the patient-centered-worded set -- but the claim that exactly items 9/13/17 misbehave, and the reproduction of published Table 1, are both unconfirmed.
